evidence_excerpts: Say that p is quasi-subsumed by q (in symbols: p ≲ q) iff there is some r such that p ∧ r ≤ q. Replacing ⊑∨ with ≤ in our original account of grounding, and ⊑∧∨ with ≲, delivers the following subsumption-theoretic analogue: (18) p1, p2, … < q iff: (i) p1 Ù p 2 Ù … ≤ q; and (ii) neither q ≲ p1, nor q ≲ p2, nor …
text: A subsumption-theoretic version of grounding says that p1, p2, and so on ground q exactly when their conjunction is subsumed by q while q is not quasi-subsumed by any of them.
